title: Split Secret Authority: Terraform operator for VPC keystore + Vault/SecretsManager federation
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Build a Terraform-native operator and reusable module that implements a 'split-secret authority' pattern for VPC/private deployments. The operator wires a customer VPC keystore (HSM-backed key material) to a secrets backend (Vault or cloud Secrets Manager) such that Redwood workloads can rotate, fetch, and recover secrets without exposing raw key material outside HSM. This work covers IaC primitives, upgrade paths for private clusters, automated health checks, and an operator reconciler for safe rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terraform module exposes inputs for HSM connector endpoints, Vault/SecretsManager backend config, RBAC bindings, and a rotation policy. 2) Operator can perform rotate/reencrypt workflow with canary rollout to a subset of agents and automatic rollback on failures. 3) Healthcheck endpoints (+metrics) surface keystore connectivity, sync lag, last-rotate timestamp, and mismatch counters in the Redwood console. 4) Integration tests validate secrets read/write with HSM-backed keys in CI and a local acceptance harness. 5) Security review completed and documented.
technical_decisions:
- Use split-authority where only key material HSM-held signs/unwraps; Vault/SecretsManager stores encrypted blobs and rotation metadata.
- Terraform module will create minimal network constructs (subnets, endpoint interfaces) and configure private endpoints for Vault/SM where available; no public endpoints by default.
- Operator implements reconciliation loop written in Go leveraging the existing infra-operator library and the Redwood keystore client.
- Drift detection via periodic checksum on Terraform state and operator reconciliation events; critical metrics emit to Prometheus using existing telemetry library.
- To minimize blast radius, initial rollout supports 'dual-write' mode followed by cutover window, with ability to opt into immediate cutover for greenfield customers.
implementation_notes: Module structure: terraform-module/secret-federation/{modules/hsm-connector,modules/vault-shim,examples/}. Provider compatibility: support AWS KMS/HSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, and generic PKCS#11 endpoints for on-prem HSMs. Operator responsibilities: watch SecretAuthority CRD, reconcile desired encryption envelopes, orchestrate canary encrypt/decrypt tests, and trigger async rotation jobs. Healthchecks: /health/keystore, /health/sync, /metrics exposing 'redwood_secrets_sync_lag_seconds' and 'redwood_keystore_unavailable_total'.
migration_plan: Stage 1: Deploy terraform module in staging with read-only mode against existing secrets to validate network and creds. Stage 2: Enable dual-write encryption where operator writes both legacy and new envelope versions. Stage 3: Run canary rotation on 1-2 agents for 24 hours, monitor metrics and error budget. Stage 4: Promote to 25%, 50%, then 100% with 24h observation windows. Stage 5: Deprecate legacy envelope versions after 30 days and provide rollback scripts. Document manual rollback steps in runbook.
testing_strategy:
- Unit tests for operator reconciler and Terraform module plan checks.
- Integration tests in CI using ephemeral cloud accounts (secrets-staging project) and on-prem PKCS#11 simulator for HSM cases.
- Chaos test: simulate HSM unavailability and ensure operator enters safe-backoff state, does not attempt to rotate, and marks customer as degraded with alert.
- E2E: create secret via API, assert envelope decrypts with HSM operation and that failover path (cached envelope) works for short outages.
observability_and_slo: Expose metrics, traces, and logs: rotate duration, last successful rotation timestamp, failed-rotation count, sync lag. Set SLO: 99.9% keystore availability for private deployments. Alerts: PagerDuty on failed-rotation >=3 in 1h or keystore_unavailable_total > 5 within 10m.
security_considerations:
- HSM private keys never leave hardware boundary; module enforces 'no-export' flags where supported.
- IAM roles scoped to minimum privileges.
- All inter-component traffic must use mTLS with short-lived certs issued by Redwood CA.
- Audit logs forwarded to central log store; retention configurable by customer.
- Security review required prior to GA.
open_questions: Should we surface per-customer KMS usage metrics in the public Console or keep them internal to billing pipelines?
Do we need to support bring-your-own-CA for mTLS in private air-gapped installs?
What is the canonical token refresh mechanism for the operator in on-prem installs where STS isn't available?

notes: This ticket intentionally avoids reusing legacy naming around 'kms-hsm' to emphasize architectural pattern 'split-secret authority' which separates signing/unwrapping authority (HSM) from storage/backends (Vault/SecretsManager). Expect follow-up tickets for provider-specific adapters.
